Toolkit

toolkit is the library every MixOS egui application is built on. It is the shell layer of the egui applications decision (see AGENTS.md §4.1). An app keeps its behaviour in a headless engine and its UI state in one serialisable struct. The toolkit draws the window around that state and routes every action through one command registry.

The UI-free registry and Fluent Strings now live in action. Toolkit keeps the egui adapter and its existing nullary command API, with the moved data types re-exported. Core and toolkit describe() emit stored chords in the keymaps grammar (Ctrl+=, ArrowLeft, or short forms), ordered Ctrl, Alt, Shift. Executed events use the command 0.2.0 v2 body with bounded params and result, and the legacy wrapper maps authorisation refusals to CommandError::Denied.

It gives each app:

  • the resolved design as an egui style, plus the embedded Inter and JetBrains Mono faces and the Lucide icons;
  • the client-side title bar, menu bars and menus, and the View › Theme submenu;
  • the chrome components (bars, buttons, panels, tabs, fields, toggles, combos, sliders, canvas scrollbars, tooltips, dialogs), drawn to the chrome specification in each chrome scheme;
  • the command registry, which generates menus, shortcuts, the palette and the Bus surface, and records every executed command;
  • the drive commands, the UI-level Bus commands that every app shares;
  • Fluent string catalogues, a key-chord grammar, and thumbnail decoding.

The source is libs/toolkit.

Who uses it

The apps term, ced, dopus, prefs, screenshot, backdrop and workshop; the editor library; and four of compd's crates (decor, ui, scene-host, world). backdrop is the only one that turns on the layer feature.

Starting an app

Call toolkit::install(ctx, &theme) once on the egui context. It installs the image loaders the icons need and applies the theme's style and fonts. Apps carry Followed::Look.ui into Theme::with_ui when following settingsd. The desktop text scale multiplies all typography and content surface fonts; density multiplies spacing and control metrics. The shared ui_scale module clamps both to the settings contract ranges and names the density steps. Reinstalling a theme replaces these values without compounding them. A window's own theme choice preserves them. Per-app text overrides are not applied because the current settings summary carries only the desktop UI values. Theme::load() reads the shared theme.conf.mix from the MixOS etc directory ($MIXOS_ETC, else $MIXOS/etc, else /etc/mixos for root, else $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/mixos). It falls back to the embedded design, and says why on stderr, when the file is missing or unusable.

A minimal window, condensed from tests/snapshot.rs:

use toolkit::action::{Command, Registry, always};
use toolkit::{Icon, Strings, Theme, icons};

#[derive(Default)]
struct Demo { refreshed: u32 }

let mut commands = Registry::new();
commands.add(Command {
    id: "bus.refresh",           // stable, never reused once published
    label: "cmd-refresh",        // Fluent key
    menu: Some("menu-bus"),      // Fluent key of the top-level menu
    submenu: None,
    group: 0,
    shortcut: Some(egui::KeyboardShortcut::new(egui::Modifiers::COMMAND, egui::Key::R)),
    icon: Some(Icon::RefreshCw),
    enabled: always,
    run: |s: &mut Demo| s.refreshed += 1,
});

let theme = Theme::load();
toolkit::install(ctx, &theme);
let strings = Strings::new(include_str!("../i18n/en/demo.ftl"));
let stroke = icons::stroke_width(&theme);

// each frame:
let _ = toolkit::titlebar::show(ui, "Demo", Some(Icon::Server), stroke,
                                &commands, &state, &strings);

Main pieces

Adopting saved window state

Use toolkit::saved::Store<MyArrangement> for each window kind. The app struct derives Serialize, Deserialize and Default and contains only passive app choices: selection, expanded tree keys, filters and view modes. Pass its own version to Store::load; a different app version resets only that section. Keep drafts, credentials, replies and live data out of it.

For a native window, pass AppDirs::resolve(app).map(|d| d.state()) as the directory. It already identifies the app: the file is <AppDirs::state()>/window.conf.mix. For another window kind, use a named subdirectory. Tests and headless runs pass an injected directory or None for memory only. Loading never creates directories.

Toolkit owns the window and widgets sections. Apply store.window.viewport(builder) before starting eframe; restore the five theme axes with store.window.theme.choice(), preserving None as follow session. After each frame, call window.capture(ctx), update the app value and theme choice, and call tick(Instant::now(), pointer.any_down()). Only changed serialised values are written, at most once per second and never while a pointer button is down. Schedule another pass only when pending() is true. Call flush() at exit. Writes use config::atomic.

Call widgets.install(ctx) once, then widgets.collect(ctx) before saving. Replace a panel's show call with saved::widgets::panel, a ScrollArea's show with saved::widgets::scroll, and a panel::group with saved::widgets::group. Give each a stable app-chosen name. Panel shares restore independently of pixels; the helper reports user resizing without feeding layout minimums back into saved shares. Scroll offsets apply once, after content lays out, clamped to its bounds; an optional content key prevents applying another selection's offset. Live trees pass ready: false until restoration is meaningful. Use forget_scroll when keeping a restored selection in view should win. collapsing saves a CollapsingState's openness.

On compd, pass the app's existing Bus call adapter to Frame::restore after the window appears. The adapter returns None for transport errors or any non-zero return code. Toolkit probes the catalogue, matches app ID and PID, and sends generation-fenced workspace then placement/maximise requests. It stops silently at a refusal and restores the prior workspace if placement failed after moving it; it never focuses or switches workspace. Before disconnecting at exit, use Frame::capture_exit to remember output, position and workspace. It reads the output origin and window geometry, so client shadows and multiple outputs do not shift the restored position. Other Wayland desktops restore only size and maximised state; no position is invented.

The strict-data envelope has schema_version: 1. Malformed files and unknown envelopes load defaults and are never overwritten. A section that fails decoding resets only itself. Store::describe() exposes the current saved values to the app's info/describe Bus response without exposing file paths.

Theme and look

  • theme: Theme holds a resolved design together with the context it was compiled for (scheme, style, mode, contrast) and its framing (server- or client-side decorations, caption side). Build one with Theme::embedded(), for_context, from_source (a full design document or a selection-only file) or load(). Then adjust it with with_choice, framed and with_overlay.
  • session_look: turns the desktop profile's appearance, as settingsd holds it, into a Theme. It is pure, with no Bus and no I/O. An appearance that names a design this build does not know leaves the app's session theme in place.
  • theme_menu: the View › Theme submenu, added with Registry::theme_menu. It covers the hue schemes (Ocean, Crimson, Stone, Forest, Sunset, Mono), the chrome schemes (Pro, Studio, Classic), modes, styles and framing. Command ids are view.theme.<scheme>, view.mode.*, view.style.*, view.decorations.* and view.captions.*, and each axis can follow the session.
  • style: maps a hue scheme's design onto egui's Style. The module docs give the field-by-field mapping table.

Window decorations default to auto. The requested mode is design::RequestedDecorations (auto, csd, ssd); Theme::decorations() returns the two-valued design::Decorations. Call toolkit::decorations::initialise(cc) in the eframe creation callback before installing the theme, so detection uses winit's actual backend. X11 uses the window manager's frame. On Wayland, a colon-separated, case-insensitive MixOS desktop name keeps the app title bar; otherwise an advertised zxdg_decoration_manager_v1 selects the desktop frame. Failure or absence keeps the app title bar. Server framing leaves only the menu-bar row inside.

MIXOS_DECORATIONS accepts these three names, ignoring case and surrounding whitespace, and overrides the app choice and then the session setting. Invalid non-empty values warn once and are ignored. Choices are still saved under an override. Detection runs lazily once per process, uses an independent Wayland connection, and gives up after a 200 ms wait budget within the 250 ms reply limit. A WAYLAND_SOCKET hand-off skips the registry check entirely. Effective Bus look maps report decorations as csd or ssd, and decorations_reason as override, choice, or rule1 through rule4. Tests can scope a design::decorations::Resolver with with_resolver, injecting both facts and the variable without reading the real session.

  • chrome: the colours and geometry of the title bar and menus. For the chrome schemes (pro, studio, classic) it supplies the whole egui style, taken from the design's chrome family. Components read Chrome::style and Chrome::metrics and never ask which scheme they are drawing, so a new style needs only design data. See the chrome family decision.
  • fonts: the embedded faces. Weight is a design token: each typography role names a weight, and the static Inter file of that weight is the one installed. Monospace is JetBrains Mono.
  • icons: Lucide icons, from unmodified upstream SVGs. The Icon enum names them. Stroke width comes from the design metric icon.stroke_width, and colour comes from the widget's text colour at draw time. See the icons and type decision.

Window chrome and components

  • titlebar: the client-side title bar. From the left it holds the app mark, the registry's menus, the centred title, an optional right-hand group of controls, and the minimize, maximize and close buttons. Captions can be on the left instead. A window opened with titlebar::viewport is undecorated. Only the free gap between the menus and the buttons drags the window. Call titlebar::edges last in the frame to add the resize zones. Under server-side decorations the row becomes a plain menu bar.
  • menu: menu bars and menus drawn by the toolkit, not by egui's MenuBar. One highlight is shared by pointer and keyboard, a menu opens on press, and press-drag-release runs an item. Nav holds the open menu and its highlights as pure data and is tested without egui.
  • bars, button, panel, tabs, field, toggle, combo, slider, canvas, tooltip, dialog: the chrome components (options, status and tool bars, icon rail, push and icon buttons, dock panel groups, document tabs, value, text and search fields, checkboxes and switches, combo boxes, sliders, canvas scrollbars, tooltip wording, and modal dialogs).
  • markdown: Markdown drawn natively. Document::parse(&str) turns CommonMark with GFM tables, strikethrough and task lists into plain data (pulldown-cmark, parser only), so an app parses once and keeps the document in its state. markdown::show(ui, &document) draws it every frame from the theme: heading sizes stepped from the Heading style, code in the monospace face on the field surface (scrolled sideways, never wrapped), quotes after a rule, lists with read-only task boxes, striped tables, rules and links. Each text run is one selectable label. Links go to Context::open_url only for http, https and mailto (markdown::openable), with the address on hover, and show returns the link clicked. Images are never fetched (the alt text links to them) and raw HTML shows as text. markdown::looks_like_markdown(&str) is a conservative test for plain text written as Markdown: one fence, table or pair of headings, or two distinct signals among a heading, a list, bold or emphasis, inline code, a link and a non-reply quote, scanned outside quoted lines and the signature. The email reader uses both.

Commands

  • command: Command<S> is one action, with an id, a label key, a menu and submenu, a group, a shortcut, an icon, an enabled rule and a run handler over the app's state S. A handler only changes state. Work that leaves the process, such as a Bus call or a file write, is queued on the state for the app's effect loop. Registry<S> provides add, add_choice, add_toggle, execute(id, state, origin), describe, menus and model, shortcuts, search, shortcut_grid and rebind. The UI, the command line and Bus commands all dispatch by id.
  • executed: every run is recorded with its Origin (menu, shortcut, palette, ui, bus, macro) and given a per-process sequence number. It goes into a bounded Journal that counts the runs it drops. Registry::take_executed hands the records to the app's Bus connection, which publishes them on <app>.action.executed (decision).
  • keymap: the chord grammar (Ctrl, Alt, Shift, then one key, joined by +). Registry::rebind applies the person's bindings from the desktop profile.

Drive commands

drive lets an agent do in the window anything a person can. drive::install(ctx, app) turns on AccessKit, keeps each pass's widget tree, and injects queued pointer and key events through egui's input hook, the same path real input takes. The app registers these commands under its own prefix (<app>.ui.tree and so on):

ui.tree, ui.click, ui.pointer, ui.scroll, ui.key, ui.type, ui.menu, ui.menu.list, ui.menu.open, ui.menu.close, ui.capture, window, window.state

The app forwards each request, with the prefix removed, to drive::request from inside a frame. It sends back whatever request, or drive::logic (called once per frame), returns. It holds later commands while drive::pending is true, and calls drive::finish before closing. Reads answer at once. Input commands run one at a time, one step per pass, and answer one pass after their last step. At most 32 input requests can be queued. The driving guide shows them in use.

viewport: "macro-editor" addresses the editor owned by the app window handling the request. Names become available on the first native child pass; an embedded editor has no separately drivable viewport. Closing one window removes only its own editor. Child requests have a ten-second deadline by default (the configured Options::capture_timeout); logic returns TIMEOUT if the child stops rendering before completing a request, so later Bus commands can proceed.

Strings, thumbnails, layer surfaces

  • strings: Strings::new(ftl) wraps an app's Fluent catalogue (i18n/en/<app>.ftl). It provides get, with (with arguments) and has. A missing key renders as the key itself, so a gap shows on screen instead of a blank. The toolkit's own labels, such as window buttons and the Theme menu, are in i18n/en/toolkit.ftl.
  • thumbnail: decodes cached thumbnail PNGs within explicit size limits on a Decoder thread, ready to upload as textures. Making the thumbnails is the job of thumbs.
  • layer (feature layer): egui programs on wlr-layer-shell surfaces, such as wallpapers, desktops and docks. layer::run(options, program) creates one surface per output (Outputs::Each), or a single surface the compositor places. Each surface has its own egui context and draws through wgpu's GL backend on its wl_surface. It follows fractional scale and takes pointer, scroll and optional keyboard input. It redraws only when something changes, so an idle surface costs nothing.

Features and dependencies

The default build has no features. layer adds smithay-client-toolkit 0.19.2 (the version eframe's winit already links), wayland-backend, wgpu, egui-wgpu and xkbcommon. Workspace dependencies: assets, config, design, settings (data types only, no Bus) and thumbs.

Assets and licences

assets/fonts/ holds static Inter (Light, Regular, Medium, SemiBold) and JetBrains Mono (Light, Regular, Medium) faces with their OFL texts. assets/icons/ holds the Lucide SVGs with LICENSE-lucide.txt, and mixos.dev uses the same icons. assets/licenses.conf.mix pins each notice by SHA-256. This includes the notices for egui's own fallback fonts, which are in assets/fonts/fallbacks/. scripts/install_licenses.mix installs them under <share>/licenses/toolkit (default share /opt/mixos/share). --check validates only the sources, and --verify checks an installed tree. See the bundled font licences decision.

Testing

Unit tests sit in the modules; for example menu::Nav is tested as plain data. The integration tests in tests/ drive real frames through egui_kittest:

  • components.rs, menu.rs, titlebar.rs, chrome.rs: component, menu and title-bar behaviour under pointer and keyboard;
  • drive.rs: the drive commands, requested inside frames the way an app's shell requests them;
  • snapshot.rs, components_snapshot.rs: offscreen wgpu snapshots across schemes and modes, compared with tests/snapshots/*.png. Regenerate them with UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1, and look at the images before committing;
  • spec_renders.rs: when CHROME_RENDER_DIR is set, it renders the chrome scenes for an out-of-tree comparison against the chrome specification's evidence. When it is unset, it does nothing;
  • asset_licenses_test.mix: install, drift and verify checks for the licence installer.

On an authorised build worker at a pushed commit:

cargo test --locked -p toolkit
cargo test --locked -p toolkit --features layer
